notes: Passages are book/chapter/verse references; scripture text is intentionally not duplicated. Guided plans include original short study notes; the full-Bible schedule contains reading assignments only. Completion and reminders should be stored separately from this catalog. Chapter-only references imply the whole chapter; endChapter is inclusive; startVerse/endVerse, when present, are inclusive.

plans.title: New to the Bible
plans.description: A seven-day introduction to the Bible’s unfolding story, from creation to Jesus and the gospel.

days.title: The Beginning
days.introduction: God creates a good world and gives human beings responsibility within it.
reflectionQuestions: What do these chapters reveal about the Creator and human purpose?
days.takeaway: Our story begins with God's creation and care.

days.title: What Went Wrong?
days.introduction: Human disobedience brings shame and alienation, while God still seeks the people he made.
reflectionQuestions: What changes after Adam and Eve disobey God?
days.takeaway: Sin harms relationships, but God does not abandon his creation.

days.title: God Calls Abraham
days.introduction: God calls Abram to trust a promise whose fulfillment he cannot yet see.
reflectionQuestions: What does Abram's response teach about faith?
days.takeaway: Faith responds to God's promises with trust.

days.title: God Delivers His People
days.introduction: God hears Israel's suffering and acts to deliver them from Egypt.
reflectionQuestions: How does God reveal his character through these events?
days.takeaway: The God of Scripture hears and rescues.

days.title: Jesus Comes
days.introduction: The Gospels introduce Jesus as both born into human history and the eternal Word made flesh.
reflectionQuestions: What do these passages claim about Jesus?
days.takeaway: Jesus stands at the center of the Bible's message.

days.title: The Good News
days.introduction: Jesus announces God's kingdom; his death and the empty tomb are central to the gospel story.
reflectionQuestions: How are repentance, the cross, and resurrection connected?
days.takeaway: The gospel calls for a response to Jesus.

days.title: Responding to God
days.introduction: Jesus speaks of new birth, and Paul explains salvation by grace through faith.
reflectionQuestions: How do these texts describe God's gift and our response?
days.takeaway: Salvation is God's gift, received through faith.

plans.title: Who Is Jesus?
plans.description: Fourteen readings exploring Jesus’ identity, ministry, death, and resurrection.

days.title: The Word Made Flesh
days.introduction: John identifies Jesus as the eternal Word who entered human life.
reflectionQuestions: What does John say about Jesus before his earthly birth?
days.takeaway: Jesus is more than a remarkable teacher.

days.title: The Promised Messiah
days.introduction: In Nazareth, Jesus reads Isaiah and announces its fulfillment.
reflectionQuestions: What kind of mission does Jesus describe?
days.takeaway: Jesus understands his work in light of God's promises.

days.title: The Son of God
days.introduction: Jesus' baptism and early ministry introduce his identity and authority.
reflectionQuestions: What do people encounter when Jesus begins to teach?
days.takeaway: Jesus' authority is integral to his identity.

days.title: The One Who Calls
days.introduction: Jesus invites ordinary people and welcomes those others reject.
reflectionQuestions: Who does Jesus call, and what does following him require?
days.takeaway: Jesus calls people to follow him.

days.title: The Teacher
days.introduction: Jesus describes the character and witness of those in God's kingdom.
reflectionQuestions: Which teaching challenges your assumptions most?
days.takeaway: Jesus teaches a different way of life.

days.title: The Healer
days.introduction: Jesus heals a paralyzed man and claims authority to forgive sins.
reflectionQuestions: Why do the religious teachers object?
days.takeaway: Jesus addresses both visible suffering and the deeper problem of sin.

days.title: Lord of the Storm
days.introduction: Jesus calms the storm and leaves the disciples asking who he is.
reflectionQuestions: Why are the disciples astonished?
days.takeaway: Jesus displays authority over creation.

days.title: Friend of Sinners
days.introduction: Jesus seeks Zacchaeus, whose response reveals a changed life.
reflectionQuestions: How does Zacchaeus respond to Jesus' welcome?
days.takeaway: Jesus came to seek and save the lost.

days.title: The Good Shepherd
days.introduction: Jesus compares his care for his people to a shepherd who lays down his life.
reflectionQuestions: What distinguishes the good shepherd from a hired hand?
days.takeaway: Jesus knows and sacrificially cares for his people.

days.title: The Bread of Life
days.introduction: Jesus points beyond material bread to the life he gives.
reflectionQuestions: What kind of hunger is Jesus addressing?
days.takeaway: Jesus offers more than temporary satisfaction.

days.title: The Resurrection and the Life
days.introduction: At Lazarus's tomb, Jesus declares his power over death.
reflectionQuestions: What does Jesus ask Martha to believe?
days.takeaway: Jesus calls for faith in him even amid grief.

days.title: The Servant King
days.introduction: Jesus washes his disciples' feet and models humble service.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jesus redefine greatness?
days.takeaway: Following Jesus includes serving others.

days.title: The Crucified Savior
days.introduction: Jesus is crucified, forgives his enemies, and entrusts himself to the Father.
reflectionQuestions: What stands out about Jesus' words from the cross?
days.takeaway: The cross reveals both suffering and mercy.

days.title: The Risen Lord
days.introduction: Jesus' followers encounter the news of his resurrection and receive their commission.
reflectionQuestions: How does the resurrection change the disciples' understanding?
days.takeaway: The risen Jesus sends his witnesses into the world.

plans.title: Learning to Pray
plans.description: Seven days learning from Jesus and the Scriptures about sincere prayer.

days.title: Teach Us to Pray
days.introduction: Jesus responds when a disciple asks him to teach them to pray.
reflectionQuestions: What priorities appear in Jesus' model prayer?
days.takeaway: Prayer can be learned from Jesus.

days.title: Pray in Secret
days.introduction: Jesus warns against performing prayer for public approval or relying on many words.
reflectionQuestions: What motivates sincere prayer?
days.takeaway: Prayer is directed to God, not an audience.

days.title: The Lord's Prayer
days.introduction: Jesus' model includes worship, daily dependence, forgiveness, and protection.
reflectionQuestions: Which request do you tend to overlook?
days.takeaway: Prayer aligns our desires with God's purposes.

days.title: Ask, Seek, Knock
days.introduction: Jesus encourages persistent requests grounded in the Father's goodness.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jesus describe the Father's response?
days.takeaway: We can bring our needs to a good Father.

days.title: Honest Prayer
days.introduction: David moves from lament and questions toward trust.
reflectionQuestions: What does this psalm allow you to say to God?
days.takeaway: Honest sorrow has a place in prayer.

days.title: Pray with Thanksgiving
days.introduction: Paul links prayer and thanksgiving with the peace of God.
reflectionQuestions: What worries could you bring to God today?
days.takeaway: Prayer and gratitude belong together.

days.title: Keep Praying
days.introduction: The apostles call believers to persistent prayer in ordinary life and hardship.
reflectionQuestions: When do these passages encourage prayer?
days.takeaway: Prayer belongs throughout the Christian life.

plans.title: Finding Peace in God
plans.description: Seven passages about trusting God during fear, uncertainty, and hardship.

days.title: When Fear Rises
days.introduction: The psalmist admits fear while deliberately putting his trust in God.
reflectionQuestions: What does trusting God look like when you are afraid?
days.takeaway: Faith can be expressed in the midst of fear.

days.title: The Lord Is My Shepherd
days.introduction: David describes God's guidance and presence even in dark valleys.
reflectionQuestions: Which image of God's care speaks most to you?
days.takeaway: God's presence gives comfort in difficulty.

days.title: Bring Your Worries
days.introduction: Jesus tells disciples to seek God's kingdom instead of being ruled by anxiety.
reflectionQuestions: What examples does Jesus use to explain God's care?
days.takeaway: Jesus invites us to trust the Father's care.

days.title: Peace in Prayer
days.introduction: Paul teaches believers to turn anxious concerns into prayer with thanksgiving.
reflectionQuestions: How can thanksgiving reshape your response to worry?
days.takeaway: Bring your concerns to God in prayer.

days.title: Peace from Jesus
days.introduction: Before his departure, Jesus promises peace unlike the world's.
reflectionQuestions: What is the source of the peace Jesus offers?
days.takeaway: Jesus offers peace amid uncertainty.

days.title: God Is Our Refuge
days.introduction: Amid threats and upheaval, the psalm declares God a present refuge.
reflectionQuestions: What does the psalm say remains secure?
days.takeaway: God is a refuge when circumstances shake.

days.title: Hope Beyond Trouble
days.introduction: Paul affirms that suffering cannot separate believers from God's love in Christ.
reflectionQuestions: Which hardship does Paul name, and what is his conclusion?
days.takeaway: God's love in Christ remains steadfast.

plans.title: Growing Your Faith
plans.description: Fourteen days on trust, obedience, spiritual growth, and perseverance.

days.title: Faith Begins with Trust
days.introduction: Hebrews introduces faith as confidence in what God has promised.
reflectionQuestions: What does this passage say about approaching God?
days.takeaway: Faith begins by trusting God's reality and promises.

days.title: Abraham Believes
days.introduction: Abram trusts God's promise despite his unanswered longing for a son.
reflectionQuestions: Why is Abram's faith significant?
days.takeaway: God calls people to trust his word.

days.title: Faith and Obedience
days.introduction: James argues that genuine faith is demonstrated in action.
reflectionQuestions: How does James distinguish living faith from empty claims?
days.takeaway: Living faith bears fruit in conduct.

days.title: Learning God's Word
days.introduction: The psalmist treasures and meditates on God's instruction.
reflectionQuestions: How can Scripture shape daily choices?
days.takeaway: God's Word forms the habits of faith.

days.title: Growing Through Trials
days.introduction: James explains how trials can produce steadfastness and mature faith.
reflectionQuestions: What is the difference between trials and temptation here?
days.takeaway: Perseverance can deepen faith.

days.title: Trust in Hard Decisions
days.introduction: Wisdom calls for trusting the Lord rather than relying solely on personal understanding.
reflectionQuestions: What does acknowledging God in your ways involve?
days.takeaway: Trust shapes how we make decisions.

days.title: Remain in Christ
days.introduction: Jesus pictures disciples as branches dependent on the vine.
reflectionQuestions: What does abiding in Christ produce?
days.takeaway: Spiritual growth depends on remaining in Jesus.

days.title: The Spirit's Fruit
days.introduction: Paul contrasts the works of the flesh with the fruit of the Spirit.
reflectionQuestions: Which fruit would you like to cultivate?
days.takeaway: The Spirit reshapes character.

days.title: Renew Your Mind
days.introduction: Paul connects worship with a transformed mind and humble service.
reflectionQuestions: How does a renewed mind affect your view of yourself?
days.takeaway: Faith changes both thinking and behavior.

days.title: Pray with Confidence
days.introduction: Jesus' priesthood gives believers confidence to seek God's mercy and grace.
reflectionQuestions: Why can believers approach God's throne boldly?
days.takeaway: Jesus makes access to God possible.

days.title: Love One Another
days.introduction: Paul describes love as essential even amid impressive gifts and abilities.
reflectionQuestions: Which description of love challenges you most?
days.takeaway: Love is central to spiritual maturity.

days.title: Be Quick to Listen
days.introduction: James calls believers to receive God's word and practice it.
reflectionQuestions: Where does James connect hearing with doing?
days.takeaway: Growing faith expresses itself in action.

days.title: Run with Endurance
days.introduction: The writer urges persistence by looking to Jesus.
reflectionQuestions: What helps believers endure hardship?
days.takeaway: Fixing our attention on Jesus sustains perseverance.

days.title: Keep Growing
days.introduction: Peter describes qualities believers should diligently cultivate.
reflectionQuestions: Which qualities build upon faith in this passage?
days.takeaway: Spiritual maturity calls for ongoing diligence.

plans.title: Understanding Salvation
plans.description: A seven-day exploration of the biblical message of sin, grace, Jesus, and faith.

days.title: The Good Creation
days.introduction: God makes human beings in his image and gives them a good place in creation.
reflectionQuestions: What was God's original design for people?
days.takeaway: Human life begins with God's good purpose.

days.title: The Problem of Sin
days.introduction: Genesis describes rebellion, and Paul explains humanity's need for God's righteousness.
reflectionQuestions: What does sin disrupt, and why do we need grace?
days.takeaway: Sin creates a need we cannot resolve by ourselves.

days.title: God's Love
days.introduction: Jesus explains God's love and the gift of eternal life through belief in the Son.
reflectionQuestions: How does this passage connect God's love and belief?
days.takeaway: God's saving initiative comes from love.

days.title: Christ Died for Us
days.introduction: Paul says Christ died for sinners and made reconciliation possible.
reflectionQuestions: What did Christ do while people were still sinners?
days.takeaway: Christ's death displays undeserved grace.

days.title: Jesus Rose Again
days.introduction: Paul identifies Christ's death and resurrection as essential to the gospel.
reflectionQuestions: Why is the resurrection indispensable to Christian hope?
days.takeaway: The resurrection is central to the gospel.

days.title: Saved by Grace
days.introduction: Paul says salvation is God's gift, not something earned by works.
reflectionQuestions: How are grace, faith, and good works related?
days.takeaway: We are saved by grace through faith for good works.

days.title: Responding in Faith
days.introduction: The apostles call people to believe in Christ, repent, and respond to the gospel.
reflectionQuestions: What responses do these passages describe?
days.takeaway: The gospel calls us to turn to God in faith.

plans.title: The Life of Joseph
plans.description: Ten days following Joseph through betrayal, suffering, wisdom, and reconciliation.

days.title: Joseph's Dreams
days.introduction: Joseph's dreams intensify tension within Jacob's family.
reflectionQuestions: How do favoritism and jealousy shape the story?
days.takeaway: Family conflict sets Joseph's story in motion.

days.title: Betrayed by Brothers
days.introduction: Joseph's brothers sell him, and Jacob believes he is dead.
reflectionQuestions: What choices make the brothers' wrongdoing worse?
days.takeaway: Human betrayal has far-reaching consequences.

days.title: Faithful in Egypt
days.introduction: Joseph resists temptation yet suffers a false accusation.
reflectionQuestions: How does Joseph respond when obedience becomes costly?
days.takeaway: Faithfulness is possible even in unjust circumstances.

days.title: God Gives Wisdom
days.introduction: Joseph interprets dreams in prison and asks to be remembered.
reflectionQuestions: Where do you see Joseph acknowledging God?
days.takeaway: Joseph points beyond himself to God.

days.title: From Prison to Palace
days.introduction: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams and is entrusted with preparing for famine.
reflectionQuestions: How does Joseph use his new responsibility?
days.takeaway: Wisdom and preparation can serve others.

days.title: The Famine Comes
days.introduction: The famine brings Joseph's brothers to Egypt without their recognizing him.
reflectionQuestions: How has Joseph's situation changed since Genesis 37?
days.takeaway: The story turns toward a difficult reunion.

days.title: Conscience and Responsibility
days.introduction: Joseph tests his brothers, who begin to face the consequences of their actions.
reflectionQuestions: What signs of changed attitudes appear?
days.takeaway: Past wrongs must be faced honestly.

days.title: A Brother's Sacrifice
days.introduction: Judah offers himself in Benjamin's place.
reflectionQuestions: How does Judah's response contrast with Genesis 37?
days.takeaway: Self-sacrifice shows meaningful change.

days.title: Joseph Reveals Himself
days.introduction: Joseph tells his brothers who he is and speaks of God's preserving purpose.
reflectionQuestions: How does Joseph hold their actions and God's provision together?
days.takeaway: God can bring preservation through human evil without excusing it.

days.title: Forgiveness and Providence
days.introduction: After Jacob's death, Joseph assures his brothers of his care.
reflectionQuestions: What does Joseph mean by God's good purpose?
days.takeaway: Joseph chooses mercy over revenge.

plans.title: The Life of David
plans.description: Twenty-one days following David’s calling, victories, failures, repentance, and legacy.

days.title: An Unexpected King
days.introduction: Samuel anoints David while God challenges assumptions based on appearance.
reflectionQuestions: What does God emphasize when choosing a king?
days.takeaway: God sees beyond outward appearance.

days.title: Serving with Courage
days.introduction: David enters Saul's service as a musician and attendant.
reflectionQuestions: How does David serve before ruling?
days.takeaway: Faithfulness often begins in ordinary service.

days.title: David and Goliath
days.introduction: David faces Goliath with confidence that the battle belongs to the Lord.
reflectionQuestions: What grounds David's courage?
days.takeaway: Trust in God shapes courageous action.

days.title: A Loyal Friend
days.introduction: Jonathan loves David despite the threat David poses to his family's throne.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jonathan demonstrate loyalty?
days.takeaway: Friendship may require costly faithfulness.

days.title: Fleeing for His Life
days.introduction: David becomes a fugitive as Saul pursues him.
reflectionQuestions: What pressures might David have faced?
days.takeaway: Faith can be tested in uncertainty.

days.title: A Chance for Revenge
days.introduction: David spares Saul's life despite the opportunity to kill him.
reflectionQuestions: Why does David refuse retaliation?
days.takeaway: Restraint can be an act of reverence.

days.title: Another Test of Mercy
days.introduction: David again refuses to take Saul's life.
reflectionQuestions: What is consistent in David's reasoning?
days.takeaway: Godly restraint may require repeated choices.

days.title: Loss and Grief
days.introduction: David mourns Saul and Jonathan rather than celebrating Saul's death.
reflectionQuestions: What does David's lament reveal?
days.takeaway: Honor and grief are not weaknesses.

days.title: David Becomes King
days.introduction: The tribes acknowledge David as king, and Jerusalem becomes his capital.
reflectionQuestions: Whom does David credit for his kingdom?
days.takeaway: Leadership brings stewardship and responsibility.

days.title: Bringing the Ark
days.introduction: David brings the ark toward Jerusalem amid joy and a sobering reminder of God's holiness.
reflectionQuestions: How are celebration and reverence held together?
days.takeaway: Worship calls for joy and reverence.

days.title: God's Covenant Promise
days.introduction: God promises an enduring royal house, and David responds with prayer.
reflectionQuestions: How does David react to God's promise?
days.takeaway: God's promises invite humble gratitude.

days.title: Kindness to Mephibosheth
days.introduction: David keeps his pledge to Jonathan by showing kindness to his son.
reflectionQuestions: What does David's action reveal about covenant loyalty?
days.takeaway: Faithfulness includes keeping promises.

days.title: David's Sin
days.introduction: David abuses royal power in his actions toward Bathsheba and Uriah.
reflectionQuestions: What choices deepen David's wrongdoing?
days.takeaway: Even powerful leaders are accountable for sin.

days.title: Confronted by Nathan
days.introduction: Nathan confronts David, who acknowledges his sin and faces consequences.
reflectionQuestions: What changes when David is confronted?
days.takeaway: Repentance begins by acknowledging wrongdoing.

days.title: A Prayer of Repentance
days.introduction: David pleads for mercy and asks God for a clean heart.
reflectionQuestions: What is David seeking beyond outward forgiveness?
days.takeaway: True repentance seeks inward renewal.

days.title: Trouble at Home
days.introduction: Violence and failures of justice fracture David's family.
reflectionQuestions: How does the narrative portray the cost of inaction?
days.takeaway: Unaddressed evil causes deep harm.

days.title: Absalom's Rebellion
days.introduction: Absalom seizes support and forces David to flee Jerusalem.
reflectionQuestions: How does David respond to losing control?
days.takeaway: Leadership may involve humility in crisis.

days.title: Grief for Absalom
days.introduction: David mourns Absalom after the rebellion ends.
reflectionQuestions: What tensions does David face as father and king?
days.takeaway: Victory does not erase personal sorrow.

days.title: A Song of Deliverance
days.introduction: David praises God as his refuge and deliverer.
reflectionQuestions: What names and images does David use for God?
days.takeaway: Remembered deliverance gives rise to praise.

days.title: Preparing the Next Generation
days.introduction: David prepares materials and instructs Solomon concerning the temple.
reflectionQuestions: How does David help a future leader succeed?
days.takeaway: Faithful leadership prepares others to serve.

days.title: David's Final Charge
days.introduction: David instructs Solomon as his life and reign come to an end.
reflectionQuestions: What does David emphasize about walking in God's ways?
days.takeaway: A lasting legacy includes a call to faithfulness.

plans.title: Walking Through James
plans.description: Seven days through the letter of James and its practical teaching.

days.title: Trials and Wisdom
days.introduction: James urges perseverance in trials and invites believers to ask God for wisdom.
reflectionQuestions: What does James say trials can produce?
days.takeaway: Faith grows through perseverance and wisdom.

days.title: Hear and Do
days.introduction: James contrasts merely hearing God's word with acting on it.
reflectionQuestions: What does James say true religion includes?
days.takeaway: God's word calls for action.

days.title: Favoritism Forbidden
days.introduction: James condemns partiality toward the wealthy in the Christian assembly.
reflectionQuestions: How does favoritism contradict love of neighbor?
days.takeaway: Faith should reshape how we treat people.

days.title: Faith That Acts
days.introduction: James illustrates why faith without corresponding action is dead.
reflectionQuestions: What examples does James use to explain active faith?
days.takeaway: Genuine faith expresses itself in deeds.

days.title: The Power of Words
days.introduction: James warns that the tongue can cause great harm and contrasts two kinds of wisdom.
reflectionQuestions: How can words reveal the condition of the heart?
days.takeaway: Wise faith changes our speech.

days.title: Humility and Tomorrow
days.introduction: James confronts quarrels, pride, judgment, and presumption about the future.
reflectionQuestions: What does it mean to submit plans to God?
days.takeaway: Humility shapes relationships and plans.

days.title: Patience and Prayer
days.introduction: James calls for justice, patience, truthfulness, and prayer.
reflectionQuestions: Where do patience and prayer appear in daily faith?
days.takeaway: Steadfast faith prays and acts with integrity.

plans.title: The Book of Proverbs
plans.description: One chapter of Proverbs each day for thirty-one days.

days.title: The Call of Wisdom
days.introduction: Proverbs 1 presents wisdom for practical decisions and character, including choosing counsel over foolish enticement.
reflectionQuestions: Where do you see choosing counsel over foolish enticement in this chapter?
days.takeaway: Seek wisdom in ordinary choices.

days.title: Wisdom Worth Seeking
days.introduction: Proverbs 2 presents wisdom for practical decisions and character, including seeking wisdom as a treasure.
reflectionQuestions: Where do you see seeking wisdom as a treasure in this chapter?

plans.title: The Gospel of John
plans.description: One chapter per day through the Gospel of John.

days.title: The Word and the Witness
days.introduction: John introduces Jesus as the eternal Word and records the testimony about him.
reflectionQuestions: What do the opening verses claim about Jesus?
days.takeaway: Jesus brings life and light.

days.title: New Life and New Worship
days.introduction: Jesus transforms water to wine and clears the temple.
reflectionQuestions: What do these signs reveal about his mission?
days.takeaway: Jesus calls for a new understanding of worship.

days.title: Born from Above
days.introduction: Jesus teaches Nicodemus about new birth and God’s love.
reflectionQuestions: Why is new birth necessary?
days.takeaway: God gives life through belief in the Son.

days.title: Living Water
days.introduction: Jesus speaks with a Samaritan woman about true worship.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jesus cross social barriers?
days.takeaway: Jesus offers living water.

days.title: Life and Judgment
days.introduction: Jesus heals a man and speaks of the Son’s authority.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jesus explain his relationship with the Father?
days.takeaway: Jesus has authority to give life.

days.title: The Bread of Life
days.introduction: Jesus feeds a crowd and teaches about the bread from heaven.
reflectionQuestions: What does Jesus ask people to seek?
days.takeaway: Jesus gives enduring life.

days.title: Division over Jesus
days.introduction: Jesus teaches at the feast and people dispute his identity.
reflectionQuestions: Why do people draw different conclusions about Jesus?
days.takeaway: Jesus calls people to discern his teaching.

days.title: The Light of the World
days.introduction: Jesus exposes the dangers of unbelief and speaks of true freedom.
reflectionQuestions: What is the difference between slavery and freedom in this chapter?
days.takeaway: Jesus offers freedom through truth.

days.title: Seeing and Believing
days.introduction: Jesus heals a man born blind amid conflict about spiritual sight.
reflectionQuestions: Who recognizes Jesus more clearly by the end?
days.takeaway: Spiritual sight involves responding to Jesus.

days.title: The Good Shepherd
days.introduction: Jesus describes himself as the shepherd who knows his sheep.
reflectionQuestions: How do his sheep recognize him?
days.takeaway: Jesus cares for his people.

days.title: The Resurrection and the Life
days.introduction: Jesus raises Lazarus and reveals authority over death.
reflectionQuestions: How does Martha express her faith?
days.takeaway: Jesus is the resurrection and the life.

days.title: The Hour Draws Near
days.introduction: Mary anoints Jesus, who enters Jerusalem before his death.
reflectionQuestions: What responses to Jesus appear here?
days.takeaway: Jesus approaches the cross intentionally.

days.title: The Servant Lord
days.introduction: Jesus washes feet and prepares his disciples for betrayal.
reflectionQuestions: What does the foot washing teach?
days.takeaway: Love expresses itself in humble service.

days.title: The Way, Truth, and Life
days.introduction: Jesus comforts his disciples and promises the Helper.
reflectionQuestions: What does Jesus promise those who love him?
days.takeaway: Jesus is the way to the Father.

days.title: Abide in Me
days.introduction: Jesus teaches about the vine, love, and the world's opposition.
reflectionQuestions: What fruit comes from abiding in Jesus?
days.takeaway: Abiding in Christ sustains discipleship.

days.title: The Spirit and Sorrow
days.introduction: Jesus promises the Spirit and speaks of grief turning to joy.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jesus prepare his disciples for hardship?
days.takeaway: Jesus gives hope beyond sorrow.

days.title: Jesus Prays
days.introduction: Jesus prays for himself, his disciples, and future believers.
reflectionQuestions: What themes shape Jesus’ prayer?
days.takeaway: Jesus intercedes for his people.

days.title: The Arrest and Trial
days.introduction: Jesus is arrested, questioned, and brought before Pilate.
reflectionQuestions: How does Jesus respond to those in power?
days.takeaway: Jesus remains steadfast as he is rejected.

days.title: It Is Finished
days.introduction: Jesus is crucified, dies, and is buried.
reflectionQuestions: What details does John emphasize at the cross?
days.takeaway: Jesus completes the work set before him.

days.title: The Empty Tomb
days.introduction: Mary and the disciples encounter the risen Jesus.
reflectionQuestions: What changes when Jesus appears?
days.takeaway: The resurrection calls for faith.

days.title: Follow Me
days.introduction: Jesus restores Peter and addresses following him.
reflectionQuestions: What does Jesus ask of Peter?
days.takeaway: Love for Jesus leads to faithful service.

plans.title: The Bible in One Year
plans.description: Read every chapter of the 66-book Bible in 365 days, with Old Testament passages daily and New Testament passages on 260 days. Books follow their canonical order within each testament.
